headline: Law renews several federal wildlife and conservation programs through 2030 and adds a black vulture permit program for livestock owners.
what_it_does: This law extends funding authority through fiscal year 2030 for several wildlife and conservation programs, including wetlands conservation, the Chesapeake Bay Program, a chronic wasting disease task force, invasive species management, and fish habitat projects. It gives the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service clear legal authority to run a program letting one public agency or Farm Bureau group per state hold a statewide permit to kill black vultures that attack livestock. It also funds completion of a national fish habitat study and database. Finally, it blocks the EPA through 2030 from regulating lead in fishing tackle under the Toxic Substances Control Act.

who_it_affects.how: They may get help protecting their animals from black vultures through a statewide permit held by a state agency or Farm Bureau organization.

who_it_affects.group: State Farm Bureau organizations and public agencies
who_it_affects.how: One per state can hold a statewide permit to manage black vultures that prey on commercial livestock.

who_it_affects.group: Anglers and makers of fishing gear
who_it_affects.how: The EPA cannot regulate lead in fishing tackle under the Toxic Substances Control Act through fiscal year 2030.

who_it_affects.group: People and groups in the Chesapeake Bay watershed
who_it_affects.how: Chesapeake Bay restoration programs, public access sites, and grant programs are renewed through fiscal year 2030.

who_it_affects.group: Wildlife agencies, landowners, and conservation groups
who_it_affects.how: Wetlands, fish habitat, invasive species, and chronic wasting disease programs that they may take part in or get grants from are renewed through fiscal year 2030.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; program authorizations run through fiscal year 2030.
